if i gave you this link what you can do about it i want some info about this account repos?

Ran 3 commands
Pulled it straight from GitHub’s public API. Here’s what’s there.

Account: nateherkai — “Nate Herk”
Created 2026-01-09, 2,158 followers, following 0, no bio/company/location/email set
18 public repos, 0 gists
Profile is basically an AI-tooling content/course channel — most repos are Claude Code / Codex skills, plugins and student templates
Repos, by stars

4,173	600	scroll-craft	JS	Agent skill for scroll-driven immersive websites; also a Claude Code plugin

3–7 each		claudewebtest, instant-ugc-app, brand-assets, fitcoach-ai-app, blender-website, dash	mixed	Small/undescribed side projects from Jan–Mar 2026
Total ≈ 12.1k stars across the account, and the top five repos are ~85% of it. Nothing is archived or a fork. Activity pattern: a burst of small app repos in Jan–Mar 2026, then from April onward the big skill/plugin releases, with the most recent being roast-room (Oct 10) and claude-code-mods (Oct 2).

What else I can do with a link like this, if useful: clone any repo and read/review the actual code, summarize a specific skill’s implementation, diff one against your own portal’s setup, pull its commit history or contributors, check open issues/PRs, or list who it depends on. Just name the repo — scroll-craft and token-dashboard are the two most likely to be relevant to what you’re building.

he is running a lot of ai things can you check can you run these stuff just yes or no or you need something additonal?

Ran 5 commands
Checked your machine against what each repo actually needs.

Your toolchain: Node 24.7, npm 11.5, Python 3.13, git ✅ — missing ffmpeg/ffprobe, gh, uv, deno, bun. No AI provider API keys set in the environment.

Repo	Can I run it?	What’s missing
token-dashboard	Yes	Nothing. Pure Python 3.8+, no pip install, no keys. Reads your own Claude Code sessions — would work on this repo’s history right now
claude-code-mods	Yes	Nothing. Plain JS mods, install as a Claude Code plugin
human-speak	Yes	Nothing. Skill files + a Python validator script
a-bunch-of-skills	Yes	Nothing — it’s just skill markdown + scripts
AIS-OS	Yes	Nothing. Markdown context framework + JS scripts
roast-room	Yes, partly	Runs in “viewer” mode with zero keys (default). Its self-driving api mode needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (~25 calls/council); /newroaster portraits need a KIE_AI_API_KEY
scroll-craft	Yes, partly	Full build works bring-your-own-assets with no key. AI image/video generation needs KIE_AI_API_KEY (paid — ~520 credits for a six-act page)
snagtime	Yes, probably	Full Next.js + Prisma app. Needs npm install, SQLite demo DB, and a few generated secrets from .env.example. No external AI keys; Google Calendar is opt-in

the 6 small ones	n/a	Undescribed personal side projects, nothing to run
Short version: 5 of them I can run right now with nothing added. 3 more run in their free/keyless mode and only need paid keys for AI generation. snagtime needs a normal install + local secrets. Only herk-edit-kit is actually blocked, on brew install ffmpeg.

Want me to start with token-dashboard? It’s zero-setup and would immediately show you where tokens are going on this portal project.

then how these people earn that much?

Searched web YouTube RPM 2026 tech AI finance niche revenue per 1000 views creator ad share vs Instagram X payouts 9 results
Fair question — and the answer is that they don’t earn it where you’re planning to post.

The platform gap is roughly 1,000×
Platform	What it pays
YouTube (tech/AI)	~$5–20 per 1,000 views, typically ~$13 US
X	~$8–30 per million impressions
Instagram	effectively nothing for feed posts
Same unit: YouTube pays about $13,000 per million views. X pays about $20. That’s not a gap you optimise your way across — it’s a different business.

So when you see an AI automation person doing well, they’re a YouTuber. Instagram and X are leftovers they repurpose into, which is literally what Nate’s pipeline does — the YouTube video is the asset, the social posts are offcuts.

But even YouTube ads are the small line
Rough estimate of Nate’s stack — these are inferred from public numbers, not verified:

Source	Estimate
AAS+ paid community (~3,100–3,500 × $99/mo)	~$300K+/mo
YouTube AdSense (43.7M lifetime views, ~$13 RPM)	~$40K/mo
Sponsorships (Hostinger, ClickUp, Lovable, ElevenLabs, n8n)	sizeable, lumpy
Affiliate/referral (Blotato, n8n, Hostinger)	recurring
Client work (“Blotato is also a client of mine”)	project-based
Instagram + X	≈ $0
The community is the business. Everything else is marketing for it. ~90% of the money comes from a thing that isn’t on any social platform.

The number that should decide your strategy
450,000 free community members → ~3,100 paying = 0.7% conversion.

Run that backwards for a $10K/month target:

Low-ticket model (his): $10K/mo ÷ $99 = ~100 members → at 0.7% needs ~14,000 free members → needs ~100K+ YouTube subscribers
High-ticket model (yours): $10K/mo = 2 client contracts at $5K → at a similar conversion rate, needs ~400 engaged followers
Same money. About 250× less audience. That’s the entire reason I keep pointing you at expertise content over news — not taste, arithmetic.

Two things nobody mentions
Timing. He started September 2024 and hit 230K in nine months. That was the n8n/AI-agent hype window, as an early mover in an exploding category with almost no competition. There are now thousands of AI automation channels. The model still works; that arbitrage doesn’t repeat.

Survivorship. For every Nate, thousands ran the identical playbook and got nothing. You only ever see the winner, which makes the strategy look far more reliable than it is.

The one transferable lesson
His content is an ad for his product, and they’re the same subject. Teach n8n → sell an n8n community. Teach Blotato → earn the affiliate commission. The content creates the exact desire his offer satisfies.

This is the real reason tech news can’t pay: there’s nothing to sell at the end of “OpenAI announced a thing.” No offer fits it. Whereas “here’s the RLS trap that silently disabled our access control” ends naturally at “…and I do this for hire” — and your contact page already exists.

Want me to map your specific path to a first $1,000, or skip ahead and start building?

These people don't earn on Instagram or X — YouTube pays ~$13 per 1,000 views where X pays ~$8–30 per million, and the real money is a paid community: roughly 3,100 members at $99/mo. That model needs a ~450K free funnel to feed it.

"""Check local readiness without printing credentials or contacting providers."""
import argparse,importlib.util,json,os,sys

def check(environ=None,policy_path=None):
    e=os.environ if environ is None else environ
    checks={'"'python_3_12_or_later':sys.version_info >= (3,12),
            'pillow_installed':importlib.util.find_spec('PIL') is not None,

# Optional GitHub Pages media staging

"'`pages_media.py` stages already reviewed slides at content-derived paths for a GitHub Pages site. It never uploads, edits a repository, enables Pages, changes DNS, or posts. Example:

```
python3 pages_media.py --carousel /path/to/approved/carousel --site-base https://YOURNAME.github.io/YOURMEDIAREPO --out /private/new-staging-folder
```

The site-base must be the exact owner-controlled HTTPS github.io Pages site. Output contains `media/<sha256>.png`, `.nojekyll`, and `urls.json`. The URL is an unverified prediction until an authorized operator deploys these files to that exact public Pages site and validates access. Publishing to Pages makes slides public before a social post, and GitHub Pages has usage/content limits; check https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits and service terms. The existing ayushtyagi.dev portfolio is not involved. Do not enable or change DNS without reviewing the site setup.

Page files can be replaced or removed by repository operators. Hashed names alone do not enforce immutability; verify served bytes using `reviewed_publish.py` immediately before submission, maintain access until Buffer retrieves them, and monitor final posting. Cache propagation can delay availability. Private drafts and secrets must never go into a public repo. The delivery loop currently only supports the R2 uploader; Pages staging and deployment are separate manual steps and not end-to-end automated. No live Pages deployment, Buffer retrieval, or Instagram publication has been tested.
EOF

# Experimental automatic delivery after review

Not deployed or live tested. This optional worker can poll for locally reviewed drafts and transfer each reviewed carousel to a configured R2 public bucket, check the publicly served image bytes match the local approval, then submit to the configured Buffer channel. Once enabled, recording a local review can eventually result in a public post without another per-post prompt. The review button itself is not a publication authorization; the owner must separately create an explicit delivery policy and start the live worker. No such policy has been created or enabled by this project.

**Requirements:** a dedicated authorized test Buffer account/channel, working free-tier or otherwise budgeted Gemini and R2 accounts, persistent private storage for the queue/drafts and both SQLite ledger tables, public R2 bucket/domain, scoped credentials, a process that stays online, and provider billing controls. R2 may require a subscription or payment method, and usage may incur charges. The existing Meta restriction and external account access remain unresolved. A max post count is not a CAD spending cap.

**Risk and limitations:** it has only been tested with fake storage and Buffer clients. Public images are exposed during upload before social publication. Other authorized writers can alter or remove images after verification; content hashes and conditional upload do not ensure permanent immutability. Buffer acceptance is not Instagram publication. The worker has no alerting, remote review, delivery reconciliation, provider interoperability, measured costs or verified end-to-end deployment. Failed upload or ambiguous Buffer outcome halts the loop for manual investigation. A crash can leave "'`pending`; no automatic retry is offered. R2 may contain partial public media. Do not delete/reset the ledger to retry; all workers must share the same durable ledger and backing files. Duplicate content with a different review digest may still be posted. Provider costs, privacy and policy requirements are your responsibility and no CAD 50 hard cap is enforced.

**Only after verifying all requirements and explicitly deciding to enable automatic posting**, create a private JSON policy file outside source control:

```
{"authorize_reviewed_to_configured_channel":true,"account_id":"R2_ACCOUNT_ID","bucket":"BUCKET_NAME","public_base":"https://PUBLIC_IMAGE_HOST","channel_id":"BUFFER_CHANNEL_ID","max_posts_per_day":1}
```

This is blanket authorization to queue reviewed local drafts to that exact channel and make their images public. Verify source facts and rights before clicking review. Set `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `BUFFER_API_KEY` securely using the chosen host'"'s secret manager, never in chat. See MEDIA_HOSTING.md, REVIEWED-PUBLISHING.md and WORKER.md. After deliberately configuring the policy and secrets, an operator can run "'`delivery_loop.py --db QUEUE_DB --root DRAFT_ROOT --policy PRIVATE_POLICY --ledger PERSISTENT_LEDGER --run-live --ack-public-media-and-cost` once; adding `--loop` polls while the process runs. #"'!/usr/bin/env python3
"""List completed review drafts and launch a local reviewer; never posts."""
import argparse,json,os,re,sqlite3,sys
from pathlib import Path
import review_server

def get_items(db_path,root):
    root=Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
    if not root.is_dir():raise ValueError('"'Draft root must be a directory')
    p=Path(db_path).resolve(strict=True)
    db=sqlite3.connect(p.as_uri()+'?mode=ro',uri=True)
    try:rows=db.execute(\"SELECT j.story_id,s.title,j.output_path FROM draft_jobs j JOIN stories s ON s.id=j.story_id WHERE j.state='review' ORDER BY j.completed_at DESC\").fetchall()
    finally:db.close()
    items=[]
    for story_id,title,output in rows:
        if not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-f]{64}',story_id):continue
        raw=Path(output)
        if raw.name "'!= story_id or raw.is_symlink():continue
        try:
            path=raw.resolve(strict=True)
            if path.parent != root or not (path/'"'receipt.json').is_file() or (path/'carousel').is_symlink():continue
            carousel=(path/'carousel').resolve(strict=True)
            if carousel.parent"'!=path:continue
            snap=review_server.snapshot(carousel)
            status='"'needs_review'
            approval=carousel/'approval.json'
            if approval.exists():
                a=json.loads(review_server.read_file(approval,review_server.MAX_TEXT))
                status='reviewed' if a.get('digest')==snap['digest'] and a.get('files')==snap['files'] else 'changed_since_review'
            items.append({'id':story_id,'title':title,'status':status,'carousel':str(carousel)})
        except (OSError,ValueError,review_server.ReviewError):continue
    return items

def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);p.add_argument('--db',required=True);p.add_argument('--root',required=True);p.add_argument('--open',metavar='STORY_ID');p.add_argument('--port',type=int,default=8765);a=p.parse_args()
    if not 1<=a.port<=65535:p.error('Invalid port')
    items=get_items(a.db,a.root)
    if not a.open:
        print(json.dumps(items,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False));return 0
    matches=[i for i in items if i['id']==a.open]
    if len(matches)"'!=1:raise ValueError('"'Story not found or output incomplete')
    server=review_server.ReviewServer(matches[0]['carousel'],a.port)
    print(f'Review at {server.origin}/. Press Ctrl-C to stop. Nothing is posted.',flush=True)
    try:server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:pass
    finally:server.server_close()
    return 0
if __name__=='__main__':
    try:sys.exit(main())
    except (OSError,ValueError,sqlite3.Error,review_server.ReviewError) as e:print('Inbox error:',e,file=sys.stderr);sys.exit(1)
PY
